title: CS-MT026-ClaudeRoleOverlayBinding

scope.summary:
GOAL: Bind Handshake Roles (machine-readable role definitions from the roles MT group: MT-081 role schema, MT-082 role injection engine) to Claude sessions at launch: the role's system-prompt overlay is injected via `--append-system-prompt-file <path>` (APPEND, preserving the CLI's own agentic scaffolding), optional subagent role definitions via `--agents '<json>'`, and every role injection is durably recorded with the FR event kinds defined by MT-161. Full replacement via `--system-prompt` is FORBIDDEN — it destroys the CLI's built-in scaffolding and is validator-rejected (MT-021 gate).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/claude_role_overlay.rs (overlay materializer + argv extension + recording calls); tests; no changes to the role schema/engine themselves (MT-081/082 own those).

SPEC:
1. `ClaudeRoleBinding { role: HandshakeRoleDefinition (MT-081 type), agents: Vec<HandshakeSubagentRoleDefinition> (MT-081 type, may be empty) }`.
2. Overlay materialization: `materialize_overlay_file(role, session_scratch_dir) -> PathBuf` writes the role's system-prompt overlay text to a session-scoped file (UTF-8, no BOM) under the session's scratch/artifacts directory (MT-001 session model provides the per-session dir), named `role-overlay-<role_id>-<session_id>.md`, and returns the absolute path passed to `--append-system-prompt-file`. File is written BEFORE spawn, fsynced, and its sha256 recorded (the recorded hash is what makes the injection auditable — the FR event carries role_id + overlay sha256, never the full text inline).
3. Argv extension: `extend_launch_args(preset_args, binding) -> Vec<String>` appends `--append-system-prompt-file <abs_path>` and, when `binding.agents` is non-empty, `--agents <json>` where the JSON is serde-serialized from the MT-081 subagent definitions (single argv element; the CLI parses it as one JSON document). If a specific named agent should be active from the start, `--agent <name>` is appended only when the binding requests it. The result must still pass the MT-021 validator (`validate_claude_interactive_args`), which continues to reject `--system-prompt`.
4. Recording: every injection emits the MT-161-defined FR event kind for role injection (fields: session_id, role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, agents_count, injected_at_utc) via the MT-029/MT-161 recording seam; the same record lands in the session persistence record (MT-006 seam already stores launch metadata — extend via its API only, not by schema edits here).
5. Failure posture: overlay file write failure, role schema validation failure (MT-081 validator), or oversized overlay (config cap, default 256 KiB — CLI argv/file limits are real) are typed `RoleBindingError` variants that FAIL the launch closed: a worker MUST NOT start without its role when a role was requested. There is no launch-without-role fallback.
6. Cleanup: overlay files are session artifacts; they are removed by the session teardown path (MT-005 supervisor owns teardown; register the path with its cleanup registry) — never left accumulating in scratch.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-081 role schema types, MT-082 injection engine seam, MT-161 event-kind definitions, MT-021 preset gate.
2. Implement materialize_overlay_file (session dir, deterministic name, fsync, sha256).
3. Implement extend_launch_args + serde --agents JSON; re-run the MT-021 validator on the extended argv.
4. Wire the FR/persistence recording via the MT-161 kinds.
5. Tests: overlay materialization (content byte-exact, sha256 stable); argv extension snapshot with/without agents/--agent; extended argv passes MT-021 validation; --system-prompt still rejected; oversized overlay fails closed; write-failure fails closed; teardown removes the overlay file; recording event carries role_id + sha256 (mock recorder assertion).
6. Live proof (typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF when CLI/login absent): launch a session with a distinctive role overlay (e.g. a sentinel instruction to always prefix replies with a marker token) and assert the first assistant turn exhibits the role behavior, proving the overlay actually reached the model.
acceptance_criteria: materialize_overlay_file writes the role overlay to a session-scoped file, fsyncs, and returns the absolute path; content is byte-exact against the MT-081 role definition and sha256-recorded.

extend_launch_args appends --append-system-prompt-file <abs_path>, optional --agents '<json>' (serde-serialized MT-081 subagent definitions, one argv element), optional --agent <name>; the extended argv passes validate_claude_interactive_args.
--system-prompt full replacement is impossible: no constructor emits it and the MT-021 validator rejection is re-proven from this MT's tests.
Role-requested launches fail closed on overlay write failure, role validation failure, or oversized overlay (typed RoleBindingError); no worker starts role-less when a role was requested.
Every injection emits the MT-161 role-injection FR event (session_id, role_id, role_version, overlay_sha256, agents_count) and lands in session persistence.
Overlay files are registered for supervisor teardown cleanup and are absent after session end (test-proven).
Live proof (or typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF): a sentinel role overlay observably shapes the first assistant turn of a real session.
proof_targets: cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml claude_role_overlay -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

LIVE (type NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF if the claude CLI or operator login is absent): sentinel-role launch; assert marker token in first assistant turn + role-injection FR event recorded with matching overlay_sha256
implementation_notes: Roles are the productized successors of the .GOV/roles/* startup inject-prompts (stub Pillar A item 2). This MT is ONLY the Claude-lane binding: role schema (MT-081), injection engine (MT-082), and event kinds (MT-161) are consumed, never redefined here. Any of those seams missing = dependency-blocked (HBR-STOP-004).

APPEND-not-replace is a hard research-based rule: full --system-prompt replacement destroys the CLI's agentic scaffolding (stub rejected-options list). The only sanctioned flags are --append-system-prompt-file, --agents, --agent. --append-system-prompt (inline string form) is deliberately NOT used: file form avoids argv length limits and quoting hazards on Windows.
--agents JSON: serialize compactly (no pretty-printing) into a single argv element; Windows CreateProcess argv quoting is handled by the process-spawn layer (MT-004/sandbox), not by pre-quoting here.
Session scratch dir comes from the MT-001 session model; overlay files must live under the session's artifacts root (external artifacts discipline), never in the repo worktree.
The sentinel live test is the Spec-Realism control: argv containing the flag is NOT proof the role reached the model; observed role behavior is.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend role-binding transport; role selection GUI is part of the roles/GUI MT groups.

target_entries: Handshake Roles on the Claude lane: how a role overlay is injected (append-only), what is recorded (role_id, overlay hash), and the no-role-no-launch fail-closed rule
Subagent role definitions via --agents: format source (MT-081 schema) and when --agent activates one by name

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: WIRED — MT-161 role-injection event kind emitted per launch with role_id + overlay_sha256.
internal_diagnostics: WIRED — typed RoleBindingError fail-closed outcomes inspectable per session.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — injection is a launch-time act, not a persistent runtime; session posture is MT-005/MT-029 territory.
risk_if_missed: Workers launch role-less or with hand-pasted prompts: no reusable Handshake Roles on the flagship lane, no audit trail of what governed a worker's behavior, and the .GOV role-protocol migration path (self-hosting roadmap) has no product landing zone.

risks: RISK-1: A role binding silently degrades to a role-less launch on file-write failure, and the worker executes an MT without its governing constraints while records claim it was role-bound.
RISK-2: Full --system-prompt replacement sneaks in as a 'simpler' path and strips the CLI's agentic scaffolding, degrading worker capability in hard-to-diagnose ways.
RISK-3: Overlay content and the recorded hash diverge (file mutated between hash and spawn), breaking the audit chain that says which instructions governed the session.
RISK-4: Malformed --agents JSON (quoting/size) crashes or misconfigures the CLI at launch on Windows argv boundaries.
RISK-5: Overlay files accumulate in scratch across thousands of sessions, leaking role text and disk.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): fail-closed typed RoleBindingError; no launch-without-role code path when a role was requested; test-proven.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): no constructor emits --system-prompt; MT-021 validator rejection re-proven here; grep proof target.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): write -> fsync -> hash -> spawn ordering in one function; the launch uses the same path object; live test matches recorded sha256 against the file the CLI read.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): serde-serialized single argv element, size-capped, spawn-layer quoting; malformed-definition rejection test.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): teardown-registered cleanup with a test proving absence after session end.

research_provenance.source: Operator-verified Claude Code CLI research 2026-07-21 (--system-prompt replace vs --append-system-prompt / --append-system-prompt-file append; --agents '<json>' subagent definitions; --agent <name>; full-replacement rejected in the WP-017 stub research basis as scaffolding-destroying) + WP-017 stub draft_scope (roles as productized successors of .GOV/roles/* inject-prompts; append-overlay layer selected approach) + grounding audit of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 (launch argv flows through CliBridgeConfig args_template 92-100 and LiveCliSpawner::spawn 2425; session artifacts/external-artifacts discipline per WP-KERNEL-012 precedent).
corrections: The task brief names --append-system-prompt-file as the overlay vehicle; the inline --append-system-prompt string form exists too but is deliberately excluded here (argv-length + Windows quoting hazards) — file form only.
